worldcombat.skill.fakeout.summary: Available as your first move in each encounter: take a short step and clap quickly, attempting flinch and interruption. Committing another move or a recorded native hit spends the opening; it returns after actual disengagement.
worldcombat.skill.fakeout.use.0: Strike first for a daze right after entering battle
worldcombat.skill.fakeout.use.1: Cut short an opening the foe is winding up
worldcombat.skill.fakeout.use.2: Clap after a short entry step
worldcombat.skill.fakeout.description.0: The slap deals about %1$s contact damage; the target's defence, type and crits are applied on the hit.
worldcombat.skill.fakeout.description.1: Step up to %1$s blocks at %2$s blocks per tick, then clap %4$s blocks forward with a %3$s-block contact radius. A whiff spends the opening too.
worldcombat.skill.fakeout.description.2: On contact, attempt %1$s of flinch through shared move and supported native attack gates. Show interruption only when an interruptible action actually ends; private Boss behavior keeps its own rules.
worldcombat.skill.fakeout.feint.on: Feint form: damage x0.85 and a longer daze (x1.35) with a 1-tick faster wind-up, at the cost of a 4-tick longer cooldown.
worldcombat.skill.fakeout.feint.off: Hard form (default): damage x1.12 but a shorter daze (x0.9).
worldcombat.skill.fakeout.timing: Range %1$s blocks; wind-up %2$s s, recovery %3$s s, %4$s PP and %5$s s cooldown. Only the first action of an encounter; disengage to regain it. Waiting while engaged does not refresh it.
worldcombat.skill.fakeout.growth.0: From level %1$s the slap power rises to %2$s.
worldcombat.skill.fakeout.growth.1: From level %1$s the slap power rises to %2$s and the daze to %3$s.
worldcombat.skill.fakeout.preference.fei: On: a lighter slap (damage x0.85) that buys a longer daze (duration x1.35), a 1-tick faster wind-up and a 4-tick longer cooldown, good for opening pressure. Off: the hard form, a heavier slap (damage x1.12) with a shorter daze (x0.9), good for a little opening damage.
Only blink in at a foe within this distance. The blink is short, so larger values often cannot reach; smaller values keep it to point-blank openings.
